result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate edge betweenness counting only paths from given sources to given targets. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Calculate edge betweenness counting only paths from given sources to given targets. title: >- [Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality_subset()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Calculate edge betweenness counting only paths from given sources to given targets. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate edge betweenness counting only paths from given sources to given targets. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L48611-L48711){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.edge_betweenness_centrality_subset( sources, targets, normalized=False, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge betweenness on a subset](../assets/graphs/edge-betweenness-centrality-subset.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the sources A and B and the target G outlined; only shortest paths from A or B to G count. Every one ends along E-F and F-G (accent, 1.00). A's single path and one of B's two run through C-E, 0.75, B's other path takes B-D-E, and A-B and C-D carry none." width="100%"} The edge counterpart of `betweenness_centrality_subset()`: each shortest path that starts in `sources=` and ends in `targets=` contributes to the edges it uses, and when a pair has several shortest paths each one counts for an equal share. The result shows which links carry the traffic between two particular sets of nodes, such as the roads between residential areas and business districts, or the interactions linking a set of receptors to a set of transcription factors. Parallel edges are separate routes and split their shared paths between them; self-loops score `0`. "Shortest" follows `shortest_path()`: hops, or total weight on a weighted graph. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [sources]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Starting nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [targets]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Destination nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, divide by `n (n - 1)`. Default is `False`, as in NetworkX; raw values are halved on undirected graphs, since each path is seen from both ends. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to measure path length by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the edge attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"edge_betweenness_centrality_subset"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as an edge attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping edge IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a node does not exist, or weights are used and one is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} One breadth-first search (or Dijkstra search, when weighted) per source, followed by Brandes's dependency accumulation in which only targets start a unit of flow (Brandes, 2008): $O(|S| E)$ unweighted, $O(|S| E \log V)$ weighted. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a diamond `A-B-D`, `A-C-D` with a tail `D-E`, the two shortest paths from `A` to `E` share the tail edge and split the two sides of the diamond: ::: {#6dd34ebc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) scores = graph.edge_betweenness_centrality_subset(["A"], ["E"], return_dict=True) label = graph.get_label_from_id {"-".join(label(n) for n in graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(e)): s for e, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'B-D': 0.25, 'A-B': 0.25, 'D-E': 0.5, 'C-D': 0.25, 'A-C': 0.25} ``` ::: ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} NetworkX's `edge_betweenness_centrality_subset()` splits the flow arriving at a non-target node equally among its predecessors instead of in proportion to their numbers of shortest paths, so its values are off wherever predecessors have different path counts. EdgeCase uses Brandes's proportional split, which agrees with counting the shortest paths directly.
